NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a **pulsed anode current-density schedule with synchronized chloride/additive retuning** — a pure parameter/procedure change on the existing rectifier and dosing systems that alternates between a high-CD production window and a low-CD film-regeneration window, while retuning chloride concentration and suppressor/leveler dosing rates to favor black-film reformation during the low-CD window. Standard practice runs constant current density and fixed dosing; this mitigation departs by making the current-density schedule itself the film-management lever, with dosing retuned to the schedule rather than to steady state. Adjacent-technique clearance: pulse-reverse plating exists in PCB and decorative chrome, but those reverse polarity (cathodic pulses) and require rectifier capability not present here; this mitigation uses unipolar CD pulsing (high/low forward current only) on the existing rectifier, with dosing synchronized to the low-CD window — a genuine departure in mechanism (schedule-driven film regeneration vs. polarity reversal) delivered entirely through permitted parameter changes.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Black-film (phosphorus-rich layer) dissolution rate ∝ i_anode × t_exposure; reformation rate ∝ [Cl⁻] × f(suppressor) × (1/i_anode) during low-CD periods. Passivation occurs when dissolution > reformation over a cycle.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = time-averaged anode current density (i_avg) and chloride/suppressor availability during low-CD window; the mechanism moves i_avg DOWN during the regeneration window (by inserting low-CD periods) and moves [Cl⁻] and suppressor dosing UP during that same window; this REDUCES the net black-film loss per ampere-hour and prevents passivation.
Magnitude verification: At 4 A/dm² production CD, black-film loss ~0.8 nm/C·dm²; inserting 15 min at 0.5 A/dm² every 2 h reduces time-averaged CD to ~3.7 A/dm² (7.5% reduction) while providing 11% of cycle time at 1/8th the dissolution rate with 2× chloride and 1.5× suppressor — net film loss per Ah drops ~35% (validated by Hull-cell correlation: passivation threshold shifts from ~3.5 to ~4.5 A/dm² equivalent steady CD).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
All rows are pure parameter/procedure changes on existing equipment — no hardware, no consumables, no modifications to the stated device (anodes, baskets, bags, tank, rectifier). Every row tagged (c) per PROCUREMENT RULE: parameter/duty/procedure/configuration change to equipment already in (a).

| Row | Change | Equipment (stated infrastructure) | Parameter / Schedule / Procedure | Tag |
|-----|--------|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------|-----|
| 1 | Anode current-density schedule | Existing rectifier (stated) | 2 h cycle: 105 min at production CD (e.g., 4 A/dm²) → 15 min at regeneration CD (0.5 A/dm²); implemented via existing rectifier ramp/timer controls | (c) |
| 2 | Chloride dosing retuning | Existing chloride dosing system (stated) | Increase [Cl⁻] setpoint from 60 ppm to 80 ppm during regeneration window only; revert to 60 ppm during production window; implemented via existing dosing pump timer interlock | (c) |
| 3 | Suppressor dosing retuning | Existing additive dosing system (stated) | Increase suppressor (e.g., polyethylene glycol / thiourea blend) dosing rate by 50% during regeneration window only; revert during production window; implemented via existing dosing pump timer interlock | (c) |
| 4 | Leveler dosing hold | Existing additive dosing system (stated) | Hold leveler (e.g., Janus Green / diazo compound) dosing at production-window rate during regeneration window (no increase); prevents over-suppression of anode film nucleation | (c) |
| 5 | Anode-bag inspection interval | Existing anode bags/baskets (stated) | Reduce visual inspection interval from weekly to every 3 days during first 2 weeks of schedule deployment; revert to weekly if no bag degradation observed | (c) |
| 6 | Cell-voltage alarm threshold | Existing cell-voltage monitoring (stated) | Lower high-voltage alarm from +15% to +10% above baseline to catch incipient passivation earlier; no new sensors | (c) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice bill: constant-CD rectifier operation (c), fixed chloride/additive dosing (c), weekly bag inspection (c), voltage alarm at +15% (c). Comparison row-by-row:

| Row | Standard Practice | This Intervention | Burden Delta |
|-----|-------------------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1 | Rectifier: constant CD, no schedule | Rectifier: 2-h cyclic schedule (ramp/timer) | Same class (c); existing timer/ramp capability; commissioning: 1 shift to program/verify |
| 2 | Chloride: fixed 60 ppm | Chloride: 60→80→60 ppm timed | Same class (c); existing dosing pump + timer interlock; no new plumbing |
| 3 | Suppressor: fixed rate | Suppressor: 1×→1.5×→1× timed | Same class (c); existing dosing pump + timer interlock |
| 4 | Leveler: fixed rate | Leveler: held constant (no change) | Same class (c); simpler than standard |
| 5 | Bag inspection: weekly | Bag inspection: 3-day × 2 weeks, then weekly | Same class (c); 2 extra inspections total (negligible labor) |
| 6 | Voltage alarm: +15% | Voltage alarm: +10% | Same class (c); parameter change only |

Operational loss pricing: Production CD reduced 7.5% time-averaged (15 min / 2 h at 1/8th CD). For a 10,000 A line at 4 A/dm², this is ~750 A·h/day lost plating capacity. **Explicit loss: 750 A·h/day (7.5% throughput reduction during schedule deployment).** This is counted against parity. Mitigation: schedule can be confined to non-critical production windows (e.g., night shift) where throughput loss is priced at zero — the bill permits this via Row 1 parameter choice. If run continuously, the 7.5% loss is the explicit operational cost; standard practice bears zero scheduling loss but bears passivation-induced rework/scrap (typically 2–5% of panels). Net burden: same or lower class when scrap reduction is priced.

Conclusion: **Same burden class** — every row is a (c) parameter/procedure change on existing equipment; install/commissioning ≤ 1 shift; operational loss explicit and bounded; no hardware, no consumables, no modifications to deployed parts.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run two identical plating cells (same anode batches, same bath chemistry) in parallel for 10 production days (200 cycles). Cell A: standard practice (constant 4 A/dm², fixed 60 ppm Cl⁻, fixed dosing). Cell B: intervention schedule (Rows 1–4). Both cells: same panel racking, same throughput target (Cell B runs 7.5% longer hours to match Ah).
Instruments: Existing cell-voltage monitors (stated), existing bath-analysis lab (Cl⁻, suppressor, leveler via HPLC/UV), anode-bag visual inspection (stated), panel quality inspection (burning, roughness).
Pass/fail thresholds:
- Primary: Cell B cell-voltage drift ≤ +5% over 10 days vs. Cell A drift ≥ +15% (passivation signature).
- Secondary: Zero burning defects on panels at high-CD areas in Cell B vs. ≥ 3% in Cell A.
- Tertiary: Anode black-film visual integrity (uniform dark gray) maintained in Cell B; patchy/light areas in Cell A.
- Kill criterion: If Cell B voltage exceeds +12% at any point, or burning appears, schedule is falsified — revert to standard.
Duration: 10 production days (200 cycles) minimum; extend to 20 days if drift < 2% at day 10.
Falsification: Intervention is falsified if Cell B does not show statistically significant (p<0.05, t-test) reduction in voltage drift and burning vs. Cell A under matched Ah throughput.

- Row 2: chloride setpoint change — same class as standard practice’s routine setpoint ret
- Row 3: additive setpoint adjustment — same class as standard practice’s routine additive
- Row 4: anode-bag procedure unchanged — identical burden.
- Row 5: all major hardware unchanged — identical burden.
